name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Redemption (1.1), the base game
description: 1.1's own rules, story and simulation as Vitomir remade them (Vitomir.Engine and Vitomir.Scripting, in bin\), keeping its own time: each frame stepped by its wall time as 1.1 steps it. Headless and, now, in a window (1.1's frame controller, Vitomir.Classic in bin\, on the program's host); the 1.1 install is the player's own (oneone). Its switches below are the players' (a dedicated host's now); every other (the harness's, a developer's, --host, --join, --name, --player-template) needs --developer.

switches.window: a window with its title bar where it was left, not full screen, for this run; nothing kept (after 1.1's -window)
switches.fullscreen: full screen for this run whatever the window's settings keep (with --size, at that size as the mode)
switches.borderless: WxH or off: a window with no title bar at that size, centred on its display, for this run
switches.size: WxH: a window of that size for this run, placed by the system and not kept (with --fullscreen, full screen at that mode)
switches.gpu: vulkan or direct3d12: the GPU's driver (by default Vulkan first on Windows)
switches.ui-layout: wide, fit or stretch: how 1.1's interface lies on the picture (wide, the 16:9 stretch, by default)
switches.menu-lettering: ours or 1.1: the menus' words in our lettering (the default) or 1.1's own pictures of them
switches.camera-up: degrees from level: how far up the game camera turns, from -20 (the base game's limit) to 0 (level with the horizon, the default)
switches.camera-steps: on or off: the game camera smoothed on steps (on by default)
switches.camera-out: times: how far out the game camera zooms, from 1 (the base game's distance) to 3 (the default)
switches.gamma: g: the picture's brightness (1 the frame as drawn, 1.4 the original's own)
switches.ffmpeg: path: the ffmpeg that decodes the films (or VITOMIR_FFMPEG)
switches.mute: the sound runs but nothing is sent to the speakers
switches.fix: name[,name...] or all: 1.1's own faults fixed for this run (the Fixes page's switches)
switches.qol: name[,name...]: quality-of-life changes on for this run
switches.no-qol: name[,name...]: quality-of-life changes off for this run
switches.menu: the title screen and the main menu, as with no switch at all, with the other switches
switches.credits: the main menu with the credits rolling
switches.new-game: straight into a new game, as the single-player menu's New
switches.load: save: start from a Vitomir save (a bare name is looked for in the game's Saves folder)
switches.devmode: 1.1's -devmode: the move command out of the Storyteller's seat, and Ctrl+P into the free camera
switches.log: level, or Category=level: how much the game's log says (repeatable)
switches.log-folder: folder: where the game's managed log folder is kept
switches.log-keep: n: how many old logs are kept
switches.diagnostics: the settings in force and where each came from, printed, then stop
switches.rules: the rules in force (the rules files' numbers), a key a line with the layer each came from, printed, then stop
switches.config: file: settings read from this file as well
switches.headless-server: a dedicated host: the network game hosted with no window and no character of its own, in a console window of its own where the host types its lines (/players, /quit, ...)
switches.port: n: the UDP port a host listens on (4994 by default)
switches.no-upnp: a host asks the router for no port forwarding (UPnP)
switches.mp-chronicle: name: the chronicle a dedicated host plays (MP_DAInn by default)
switches.moderated: a dedicated host's game made with Storyteller moderation
switches.no-auto-st: a dedicated host's game without the automatic Storyteller
switches.game-name: text: the game's name in the players' lists
switches.password: text: the game's password, a host's or a joining player's (never written in a log, the console or a tape: ****)
switches.max-players: n: how many players a dedicated host lets in, itself among them (1 to 8, 8 by default, as 1.1)
switches.streamer: streamer mode for this run: network addresses and ports, the user's folder in paths and any join code hidden wherever they would show on screen (the log window too; the log files keep them). The setting is the platform's, the same in every game, and kept from the game's options
switches.log-bundle: the logs, the network trace of the last session and this machine's build and data fingerprints zipped into the game's folder for a friend to send (as /bundle on the chat line), then stop
